summary.title: Latency, Throughput, and Port Usage Information
summary.one_liner: uops.info is a reference site giving measured latency, throughput, and port usage data for x86 instructions across many Intel microarchitectures, with each value linked to its microbenchmark.
keywords: how many cycles does an instruction take
which execution port does an instruction use
takeaways: The site covers latency, throughput, and port usage for most x86 instructions on many recent Intel microarchitectures.
Much of this data is not in the official processor manuals, so the site fills that gap.
A machine-readable XML file is available, including operand information for each instruction.
An interactive HTML table lets you compare microarchitectures, with links to per-entry detail pages.
Each entry links to its microbenchmark, so values can be re-run.
summary.summary: The page is the landing page for uops.info, a site with over 800,000 detail pages of latency, throughput, and port usage data for most instructions on many recent x86 microarchitectures. It offers a machine-readable XML download with operand details and an interactive HTML table for comparing microarchitectures. The data is described as measured, and the page points to a paper by Andreas Abel describing the methodology for Intel microarchitectures. The page text does not give details on the measurement method beyond that.
